summary.short: Utah HB 148 (2024) amends Utah's criminal code on sexual images: it redefines child and vulnerable-adult sexual abuse material, criminalizes distributing intimate images without consent, and adds an offense for distributing counterfeit (edited) intimate images, effective May 1, 2024.
summary.long: HB 148 (2024) amends Utah's criminal code on sexual images. Section 1 amends the definitions in 76-5b-103, including child sexual abuse material, which covers images created, adapted or modified to appear that an identifiable minor is engaging in sexually explicit conduct, and vulnerable adult sexual abuse material. Section 2 amends 76-5b-203 to make it an offense to knowingly distribute an intimate image of an adult without consent where the distribution causes or would cause emotional distress or harm, subject to listed exceptions; the base offense is a class A misdemeanor, and a third degree felony on a second or subsequent conviction. Section 3 amends 76-5b-204 on sexual extortion, with penalties for adult actors ranging from third degree to first degree felonies depending on the victim and aggravating circumstances. Section 4 adds 76-5b-205, unlawful distribution of a counterfeit intimate image (an edited or altered depiction of an identifiable individual's likeness), a class A misdemeanor, with an aggravated offense where the depicted individual is a child. Sections 2 and 4 exempt internet service providers, interactive computer services and hosting companies under stated conditions; hosting companies must remove counterfeit images immediately upon notice to keep that exemption. The text does not mention artificial intelligence. Effective date: May 1, 2024.

relations.note: Four sections amended, each restated in full in the bill. The document carries no underlining or brackets, so new text cannot be told apart from unchanged text.

notes: Effective date is May 1, 2024 (Section 5). Only the four amended sections are included; the other Utah Code sections cited are not in the document. Internal inconsistency: 'Sexually explicit conduct' is defined in 76-5b-103(10) and again in 76-5b-203(1)(a)(ii) with different wording (e.g., 103(10)(e) 'lascivious exhibition' and 103(10)(f) 'for the purpose of causing sexual arousal'; 203 uses 'exhibition' and has no arousal limb). 76-5b-204 and 76-5b-205 incorporate the 203 definition. The 76-5b-103(2) definition of 'Distribute' ends with 'or otherwise transfer .' and is reproduced as printed. Other intra-code cross-references (76-1-101.5, 76-1-401, 76-5-111, 76-5-111.4, 76-5-404.1) are not recorded as relations.

obligations.summary: Prohibits distributing an intimate image of an adult (18 or older) without consent, where the distribution would cause a reasonable person emotional distress or harm, and the image was obtained under a reasonable expectation of privacy. Subsection (2)(b) removes the actual-harm element in listed circumstances. Applies to the amended section 76-5b-203 offense.

evidence.quote: An actor commits the offense of distribution of an intimate image if:

obligations.summary: Prohibits sexual extortion: communicating or causing threats (to the victim's person, property or reputation, or to distribute an intimate image) with intent to coerce sexual contact, sexually explicit conduct or production of images, or to obtain a thing of value. Subsection (2)(b) lists aggravating circumstances.

evidence.quote: An actor commits the offense of sexual extortion if the actor:

obligations.summary: Prohibits knowingly or intentionally distributing a counterfeit intimate image (edited or altered to depict an identifiable individual's intimate parts or sexually explicit conduct) without that individual's consent, where the image was created or provided without the depicted individual's knowledge and consent. Subsection (2)(b) makes it aggravated when the depicted individual is a child and the actor is 18 or older.

evidence.quote: An actor commits the offense of unlawful distribution of a counterfeit intimate image if the actor knowingly or intentionally distributes a counterfeit intimate image

obligations.summary: Condition for the hosting-company exemption from Section 76-5b-205: the hosting company must immediately remove a counterfeit intimate image upon notice from a law enforcement agency, prosecutorial agency, or the depicted individual. The exemption also requires no intentional aiding or abetting and no excess fee. Hosting company is defined by reference to Section 76-10-1230, which is not in this document.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies only if the hosting company meets all conditions of Subsection (5)(b) to claim the exemption from Section 76-5b-205

evidence.quote: the hosting company immediately removes the counterfeit intimate image upon notice from a law enforcement agency, prosecutorial agency, or the individual purportedly depicted in the counterfeit intimate image.

enforcement.max_penalty_text: Class A misdemeanor; third degree felony on a second or subsequent conviction for an offense under this section that does not arise from a single criminal episode
enforcement.penalty_formula: Base offense: class A misdemeanor. Second or subsequent conviction not arising from a single criminal episode: third degree felony. Penalty amounts are not stated in this text.

evidence.quote: A violation of Subsection (2) is a class A misdemeanor.

enforcement.triggered_by: Sexual extortion under Subsection (2)(a) or (2)(b) of 76-5b-204, with tiers depending on actor age, victim status and aggravating circumstances
enforcement.max_penalty_text: For an adult actor: third degree felony (Subsection (2)(a)); second degree felony (Subsection (2)(b), adult victim); first degree felony (Subsection (2)(b), child or vulnerable adult victim). For a child actor: class A misdemeanor (Subsection (2)(a)); third degree felony (Subsection (2)(b)) if there is more than a two-year age gap between actor and victim
enforcement.penalty_formula: Adult actor: (2)(a) third degree felony; (2)(b) second degree felony where victim is an adult, first degree felony where victim is a child or vulnerable adult. Child actor: (2)(a) class A misdemeanor; (2)(b) third degree felony if more than a two-year age gap. A separate offense is committed for each victim and for each separate time a victim is subjected to the offense in Subsection (2)(a). Penalty amounts are not stated in this text.

evidence.quote: A violation of Subsection (2)(a) is a third degree felony.
